episodes.204000: A cluster of storms moving across north-central and northeast South Dakota generated widespread strong winds during the early morning hours. Numerous weather stations across the area recorded gusts between 60 and 70 mph.
episodes.204020: A low pressure system from western Canada dropped into the area, creating an unstable environment with sufficient upper level wind shear for severe thunderstorms to develop. Some severe wind gusts caused damage to some buildings.
episodes.204206: An upper level weather disturbance moved through the region on August 8th. This combined with sufficient daytime heating, instability in the atmosphere to produce showers and thunderstorms. There was enough dry air in the atmosphere that any of the showers that developed were able to produce wind gusts across portions of the Oklahoma Panhandle. A few of these wind gusts occurred as a result of heat bursts that occurred as showers diminished overnight on the 8th.
episodes.205363: Thunderstorms developed across NW Kansas and led to hail up to 2 inches in diameter in Bird City, along with wind damage in Cheyenne county. Additional severe wind gusts were recorded in Rawlins county as well.
episodes.205370: A single thunderstorm developed in northern Thomas county and moved east into northern Sheridan and southern Decatur county.  A wind gust of up to 63 mph was reported from this thunderstorm.
episodes.205371: A shower developed and collapsed on the northern portion of McCook during the morning hours on the 8th where an estimated 65 mph wind gust occurred.
episodes.205481: A QLCS type mesoscale convective system brought widespread severe thunderstorm winds to eastern ND, along with, multiple brief tornadoes during the early morning hours.
episodes.205488: A QLCS type mesoscale convective system brought widespread severe thunderstorm winds to northwest Minnesota during the early morning hours. A tornado associated with this MCS also tracked from Grand Forks, ND to East Grand Forks, MN.
episodes.205570: Another round of locally heavy rain across the Upper Big Sioux Basin resulted in downstream minor flooding along portions of the Middle Big Sioux River.
episodes.205627: A stalled front and high moisture across the area combined with slow storm motion produced locally heavy, briefing flooding rainfall.
episodes.206021: A very unstable environment was in place over western and central North Dakota which combined with very strong deep layer shear to produce widespread severe thunderstorm wind gusts along with some large hail over western and central North Dakota. To start the episode, a pair of upper level short-wave troughs approached North Dakota from Montana. The first trough had limited storm develop due to a capped atmosphere, though one storm did strengthen enough to produce one-inch diameter hail over Rolette County. Storms primarily developed as the second trough approached. Initially, storms produced a mix of large hail and strong wind gusts, but as the episode evolved and the storms moved east, very strong wind gusts became the primary concern by late evening. Significant damage occurred at multiple locations, with the two most notable events occurring in Stutsman County. In Jamestown, significant damage occurred over the southern part of the city, primarily to trees. Damage also occurred to some homes and buildings. To the north of Courtenay, a farm suffered significant damage to buildings and grain handling equipment. Winds at both locations were estimated at 100 mph, with both locations also suffering significant damage during the June 20, 2025 derecho event.
episodes.206610: Late afternoon and early evening storms associated with a surface trough over the peninsula coupled with a weakness aloft over the state produce a landspout near Seffner in Hillsborough County and street flooding near New Port Richey in Pasco County.
episodes.206620: The remnants of a weak mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) propagated south over the Mississippi River in the early afternoon hours. The lift from the MCV combined with instability and increasing tropical moisture, resulted in a few showers and thunderstorms. Coverage was isolated. The increasing moisture fueled torrential downpours over urbanized areas, leading to a quick flash flooding threat.
episodes.206765: A complex of thunderstorms developed over the Red River Valley region during the early morning hours of the 8th and pushed into central and northeastern Minnesota during the mid to late morning hours. The storms intensified as they moved into the Brainerd Lakes region with bowing segments producing strong winds. By the late morning hours, the storms outran their support leading to a quick drop in intensity as they reached Lake Superior and northwestern Wisconsin. Numerous reports of tree damage were received from the Brainerd Lakes area into Aitkin and St. Louis counties. A lightning strike at a cemetery damaged headstones as well.
episodes.206902: A front nearby along with moderate instability and deep moisture led to an environment capable of producing heavy rainfall across Southeast Georgia.
episodes.207164: Saturated soils and heavy rain at the moment resulted in a small landslide in Utuado, which carried a tree and got it tangled between power lines.
episodes.207221: A severe thunderstorm brought large hail and damaging winds to portions of Gogebic County during the evening of the 8th.
episodes.207223: A series of strong thunderstorms produced gusty winds over northern Lake Superior and near Isle Royale during the morning of the 9th.
episodes.207231: A typical summertime pattern was in place across the region. The very warm waters in nearshore and tidal lakes provide a unique mesoscale environment which promotes nocturnal thunderstorm development. A waterspout developed along the outflow boundary of that storm and dissipated as it reached the coast.
episodes.207306: Many thunderstorms occurred across southeast MT, producing gusts up to 79 mph and hail sizes up to 1.75 inches. This event caused medium sized tree limbs to be snapped off, and caused extensive damage around Billings.
episodes.208186: Hot and very humid air mass in place created an unstable environment, which, in the presence of the Lake Huron lake breeze and a subtle stationary boundary stretching from the Keweenaw Peninsula to northern Lake Huron, was able to support development of scattered strong to severe storms across parts of northeast Lower Michigan during the late afternoon on the 7th, resulting in primarily large hail reports.
episodes.208187: Hot and very humid air mass in place created an unstable environment, which, in the presence of the Lake Huron lake breeze and a subtle stationary boundary stretching from the Keweenaw Peninsula to northern Lake Huron, was able to support development of scattered strong to severe storms across parts of northeast Lower Michigan during the late afternoon on the 7th, resulting in primarily large hail reports.
episodes.208188: The unseasonably hot and humid air mass persisted into the 8th, resulting in development of additional storms driven primarily by daytime heating across northeast Lower Michigan, where low-level convergence was maximized by the lake breeze boundary as well as a very weak surface trough. The most robust storms developed some rotation, indicated by reports of a wall cloud near Rose City, MI, as well as large hail up to the side of golf balls, along with heavy rain.
episodes.208189: An area of storms developed in a hot and very humid air mass and rode down a subtle surface boundary through the eastern UP during the early morning hours on the 8th, producing mainly heavy rain and some gusty winds.

Significant damage, primarily to trees, occurred over the southern part of Jamestown. The area with the greatest damage was generally between Foxtrot Road on the west and and 10th Avenue East on the east, resulting in a path length of approximately |two miles. The width of the greatest damage stretched from near 17th Street on the south end to around 11th Street on the north, approximately one-half mile. At the start of the greatest damage in the vicinity of Meidinger Park and areas south, a pontoon boat was flipped, a tree was uprooted, multiple smaller trees were either snapped or had significant branches broken off, and a camper was pushed off its blocks. Towards the east near the intersection of 14th Avenue SW and 17th Street SW, a manufactured home had its roofing material uplifted, and large spruce trees were uprooted. Continuing east passing over the Interstate 94 Business Loop, multiple trees were uprooted including spruce trees along the loop. Further east along 17th Street SE, the metal roof panels blew off the east side of a building towards the northeast and across the road. At McElroy Park and areas surrounding, many trees were uprooted, with some|smaller to medium size trees snapped. To the east near the intersection of 14th Street SE and 8th Avenue SE, an L-shaped building had its east side roofing panels blown off.
Power lines were down in the yard. Parts of a shop roof that was recently installed were torn off. Other items were blown around throughout the yard.

Significant damage occurred to buildings and grain handling equipment. Two newer pole-barn buildings had a significant portion of the structure destroyed with collapsed walls and roofs. The damage was primarily on the west side of both buildings, with farm equipment damaged inside. Another large building had multiple roof panels on its east side blown off. Multiple grain bins were damaged, one suffering very significant damage to its roofing structure. A large grain dryer was toppled when the grain leg system collapsed.

A tornado produced intermittent EF-0 and EF-1 damage in Grand Forks, ND and East Grand Forks, MN. It initially touched down near the intersection of 38th St. and 32nd Ave where it bent a light pole from the top of the intersection stop lights. It tracked to the northeast just south of Altru Hospital along 17th Ave S., past Lewis and Clark elementary School, and then crossed the Red River of the North at Lincoln Drive Park into Minnesota. It lifted over the southern part of East Grand Forks, MN around the Red Lake River near Folsom Park. Most of the damage was to trees along the path. Maximum rating is EF-1 in Grand Forks County, with wind speed at 100 mph based on snapped hardwood tree damage in Grand Forks, ND.

This tornado was likely rain wrapped intermittently produced EF-1 damage across its nearly 4 mile long path with wind speeds up to 110mph.  The tornado initially touched down about 1.5 miles northwest of the Grand Forks International Airport tracking northeast and eventually crossing I-29 before lifting just before the Red River of the North. A mobile home was rolled on its side with a person inside that needed rescued, multiple homes garages were destroyed, and wood poles were damaged on electrical transmission lines.

A tornado produced intermittent EF-0 and EF-1 damage in Grand Forks, ND and East Grand Forks, MN. It initially touched down near the intersection of 38th St. and 32nd Ave in Grand Forks, ND where it bent a light pole from the top of the intersection stop lights. It tracked to the northeast just south of Altru Hospital along 17th Ave S., past Lewis and Clark elementary School, and then crossed the Red River of the North at Lincoln Drive Park into Minnesota. It lifted over the southern part of East Grand Forks, MN in western Polk County around the Red Lake River near Folsom Park. Most of the damage was to trees. The maximum rating for the tornado was EF-1 in Grand Forks County ND. The rating in Polk County is EF-0 based on a max wind estimated at 80 mph winds from hardwood tree damage before it dissipated in East Grand Forks, MN.
